title: Shennaghys ry akin
description: Ten short stories about history you can touch: a re-enactment at Castle Rushen, a Norse house dug up near Peel, an old gospel book at Rushen Abbey, an exhibition of old alphabets, a day at the folk village in Cregneash, letters from an internment camp, an old hotel made new, a rocket and a golf ball in a space exhibition, a naturalist's cabinet in a museum, and the old feathered shuttlecocks of a badminton champion.

lessons.title: Yn aayannoo ec y chashtal
lessons.summary: Wilhelmina Ashcombe leads a re-enactment group at the castle in Castletown; fourteen-year-old Ninian Halloran wants to join, though he has no acting experience. He arrives in sandals, so she gives him heavy leather boots and the part of a young soldier born in Castletown in 1635; she shows him an old naval gun from a warship, keeps the gunpowder to herself, and at the end of the fine day the soldiers shout and the gun fires.
lessons.text:
Ta Wilhelmina Ashcombe ny stiureyder er possan aayannoo ayns Balley Chashtal. Dagh blein, ayns y tourey, ta'n possan jannoo aayannoo mooar ec y chashtal shenn. Ta ny oltee ceau eaddagh veih'n vlein 1651, as t'ad jannoo reddyn myr va sleih jannoo ad 'sy traa shen. Ta'n theay çheet dy akin ad.

Er y chied laa jeh'n aayannoo, haink guilley aeg dys y chashtal. She Ninian Halloran yn ennym echey, as v'eh kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash.

“Ta mee laccal goaill ayrn 'syn aayannoo,” dooyrt Ninian. “Cha nel aghteyrys erbee aym, agh s'mie lhiam shennaghys.”

“Cha nel feme ayd er aghteyrys,” dooyrt Wilhelmina. “Cha nel shin jannoo drama ayns theater. Ta shin jannoo bea ny sleih shenn reesht, myr v'ee. Agh ta feme ayd er eaddagh kiart.”

Va carraneyn er cassyn Ninian. Ren Wilhelmina gearey.

“Cha row carraneyn ec sidooryn 'sy vlein 1651,” dooyrt ee. “Va bootysyn trome oc, jeant jeh crackan. Gow ny bootysyn shoh.”

Hug ee bootysyn as cooat jiarg da. Va ny bootysyn mooar as trome, agh v'ad braew. Dooyrt Wilhelmina dy beagh Ninian ny sidoor aeg 'syn aayannoo: guilley va behrt ayns Balley Chashtal 'sy vlein 1635, as v'eh shey bleeaney jeig d'eash 'sy vlein 1651.

Va gunn mooar shenn er boalley y chashtal. “She gunn lhuingyssagh eh,” dooyrt Wilhelmina. “Va'n gunn shoh er lhong caggee. Hooar ad eh ass y faarkey lurg caggey lhuingyssagh, as hug ad eh ayns shoh.”

“Vel poodyr ayns y gunn?” dooyrt Ninian.

“Bee beggan dy phoodyr ayn jiu,” dooyrt ee, “agh cha bee bluckan ayn. Ta'n poodyr ayns kishtey, as ta mish goaill ymmyd jeh'n phoodyr my lomarcan. Ny bean rish!”

Haink y theay 'syn astyr, as v'eh ny laa braew, grianagh, gyn bodjal 'sy speyr.Hass ny sidooryn ayns linney. Ren Wilhelmina yllee: “Sidooryn, shass!” Ren Ninian yllee marish ny sidooryn elley, cho ard as v'eh abyl. Eisht, hug Wilhelmina aile da'n phoodyr. Va sheean mooar ayn, as va jaagh bane er y voalley. Ren y theay yllee as gearey.

“Ren oo yllee dy braew,” dooyrt Wilhelmina rish Ninian. “Bee oo ayns shoh reesht y nah vlein?”

“Bee,” dooyrt Ninian. “Agh cha jig mee lesh carraneyn.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta stiureyder y phossan aayannoo?
She Wilhelmina Ashcombe stiureyder y phossan aayannoo.
Vel aghteyrys ec Ninian?
Cha nel. Cha nel aghteyrys erbee echey, agh s'mie lesh shennaghys.
Cre'n fa nagh row ny carraneyn mie?
Cha row carraneyn ec sidooryn 'sy vlein 1651; va bootysyn trome oc, jeant jeh crackan.
Raad va'n sidoor aeg behrt?
V'eh behrt ayns Balley Chashtal 'sy vlein 1635.
Cre'n gunn va er boalley y chashtal?
She gunn lhuingyssagh v'ayn, veih lhong caggee.
Row'n laa grianagh?
Va. V'eh ny laa braew, grianagh, gyn bodjal 'sy speyr.
Cre ren Ninian marish ny sidooryn elley?
Ren eh yllee: “Sidooryn, shass!”

lessons.title: Y kere ass y thalloo
lessons.summary: The researcher Augustin Strand leads a dig at a tenth-century house near Peel, and the student Maud Kettering comes for her first day: the dig is marked out with ropes tied to sticks, the stones of the walls are exposed, and a heap of household rubbish by the door shows the common dish of the people who lived there. Maud measures each find against a red and white rod, finds a brass button, and then a bone comb with runes on it, which go to the museum in Douglas.
lessons.text:
Ta Augustin Strand ny ronseyder ass Doolish. Ayns y tourey, t'eh stiurey toghailt ayns magher faggys da Purt ny h-Inshey. Fo'n thalloo 'sy vagher shen, ta thie shenn veih'n jeihoo eash.

Er y chied voghrey jeh'n toghailt, haink studeyr aeg, Maud Kettering, dys y vagher. Va Maud feed blein d'eash, as cha row ee rieau ec toghailt roie.

Hoilshee Augustin y boayl da Maud. Va tead mygeayrt y toghailt, sniemmit rish maidjey ec dagh corneil. “Ny gow harrish y tead sniemmit,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n thalloo çheusthie jeh'n tead feer scanshoil.”

Va claghyn ny boallaghyn anchoodit nish. Va ad fo'n thalloo rish thousane blein, agh nish v'ad anchoodit 'sy ghrian. Va'n dorrys anchoodit neesht, as yn ynnyd raad va'n aile.

Ec y dorrys, va carnane mooar jeh claghyn beggey, craueyn as shliggyn. “Trustyr thieoil eh shoh,” dooyrt Augustin. “Va ny sleih va cummal 'sy thie ceau yn trustyr oc magh ec y dorrys. S'mie lhiam trustyr thieoil, son t'eh ginsh dooin c'red va ny sleih gee.”

Ayns y trustyr, hooar Maud craueyn eeast as craueyn muc. “Va eeast as feill muc ny lhongey cadjin oc,” dooyrt Augustin. “Va'n lhongey shen jeant er yn aile, çheusthie jeh'n thie.”

Va slat ec Augustin, jiarg as bane. Va dagh ayrn jeh'n slat jeih kentimeader er lhiurid. “Dagh nhee ta shin geddyn, ta shin coyrt y slat rish, as goaill jalloo jeh,” dooyrt eh. “Eisht ta fys ain er mooadys y nhee.”

Ec y vean-laa, hooar Maud cramman beg 'sy thalloo. “C'red ta shoh?” dooyrt ee. V'eh glass, agh tra ghlen ee eh, honnick ee dy row eh jeant jeh prash. “She cramman veih cooat eh,” dooyrt Augustin. Hug ad y slat rish y cramman, as ghow ad jalloo.

'Syn astyr, hooar Maud nhee elley: kere beg, jeant jeh craue. Va feeacklyn y kere ooilley ayn, bunnys. Hug Augustin y kere fo'n soilshey as jeeagh eh er dy mie.

“Ta roonyn er y kere!” dooyrt eh. “Ta ny roonyn shoh screeuit ayns çhengey ny sleih veih'n twoaie. T'ad gra: ‘Ren Thorketil y kere shoh.’”

Hie y kere as y cramman dys y thie tashtee ayns Doolish. Nish, ta'n theay abyl fakin y kere lesh ny roonyn er, as ta Maud goll dys y thie tashtee dy mennick dy akin eh.

Feyshtyn:
Raad ta'n toghailt?
Ta'n toghailt ayns magher faggys da Purt ny h-Inshey.
Vel claghyn ny boallaghyn anchoodit nish?
Ta. Va ad fo'n thalloo rish thousane blein, agh t'ad anchoodit nish.
Cre va mygeayrt y toghailt?
Va tead sniemmit rish maidjey ec dagh corneil.
Cre va ayns y trustyr thieoil?
Va claghyn beggey, craueyn as shliggyn ayns y trustyr thieoil.
Cre va'n lhongey cadjin oc?
Va eeast as feill muc ny lhongey cadjin oc.
Cre'n fa ta Augustin coyrt y slat rish dagh nhee?
Ta fys ocsyn eisht er mooadys y nhee.
Cre va er y kere?
Va roonyn er y kere: “Ren Thorketil y kere shoh.”

lessons.title: Lioar y sushtal
lessons.summary: Erasmus Larkham, a retired man who shows visitors round the ruins of Rushen Abbey in Ballasalla, takes his eleven-year-old granddaughter Zinnia there one Saturday: he explains the abbot who led the monks, the big church window and the old hazel where the garden was, then in the little museum shows her a copy of a gospel book from the abbey, with notes by a theologian and a curse on anyone who takes the book; the monks believed in such curses, but they left in 1540 and never came back.
lessons.text:
Ta Erasmus Larkham three feed as jeih bleeaney d'eash, as t'eh cummal ayns Balley Salley. Dagh Jesarn, t'eh soilshaghey Mannishter Rushen da'n theay. Jiu, haink yn inneen-vac echey, Zinnia, marish. Ta Zinnia nane jeig d'eash.

Cha nel agh boallaghyn as claghyn er-mayrn jeh'n vannishter nish. “Va braaraghyn cummal ayns shoh rish ny smoo na three cheead blein,” dooyrt Erasmus. “Va abb oc. She'n abb va stiurey ny braaraghyn. Va'n abb ny ghooinney scanshoil ayns Mannin ooilley, as v'eh ny oltey jeh'n choonseil ec y ree.”

Hie ad dys boalley mooar. Va towl mooar ard 'sy voalley. “Va uinnag vooar ayns shoh,” dooyrt Erasmus. “Cha nel glonney erbee 'syn uinnag nish, agh ta ny claghyn mygeayrt ee ayn foast. Va ny braaraghyn ooashlaghey Jee ayns yn agglish shoh, shiaght keayrtyn dagh laa, as va'n soilshey çheet stiagh trooid yn uinnag.”

“Vel sleih ooashlaghey Jee ayns shoh nish?” dooyrt Zinnia.

“Ta, keayrt 'sy vlein,” dooyrt Erasmus. “Ta saggyrt çheet, as ta sleih ooashlaghey Jee ayns shoh reesht, fo'n speyr.”

Raad va garey ny braaraghyn, va coull shenn gaase. “Va coull ayns shoh neesht ayns traa ny braaraghyn,” dooyrt Erasmus. “Hooar ronseyderyn cro coull 'sy thalloo. Va ny braaraghyn gee ad.”

Eisht hie ad stiagh 'sy thie tashtee beg. Ayns kishtey glonney, va lioar ry akin. “She coip eh shoh,” dooyrt Erasmus, “jeh lioar y sushtal veih'n vannishter. Va'n sushtal screeuit ayns Ladjyn, er laue. Ren jeeaghteyr veih'n vannishter screeu reddyn mychione y sushtal ayns oirr ny duillagyn. Va'n jeeaghteyr shen ny ghooinney ynsit.”

Ec jerrey y lioar, va focklyn screeuit ayns jiarg. “Ta mollaght ayn,” dooyrt Erasmus. “T'eh gra: ‘Mollaght er quoi erbee ta goaill y lioar shoh ersooyl.’ Va lioaryn feer deyr 'sy traa shen.”

“Chreid ny braaraghyn ayns mollaghtyn?” dooyrt Zinnia.

“Chreid,” dooyrt Erasmus. “Chreid ad dy row pooar ec mollaght. Cha nel mish credjal ayn, agh chreid sleih ooilley ayn 'sy traa shen.”

“Cre haghyr da ny braaraghyn?”

“'Sy vlein 1540, ren y ree y vannishter y ghooney. Hie ny braaraghyn ersooyl, as cha daink ad erash dy bragh.”

Jeeagh Zinnia er y lioar rish tammylt liauyr. “Bee mee cooinaghtyn er y laa shoh son dy bragh,” dooyrt ee.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va stiurey ny braaraghyn?
She'n abb va stiurey ny braaraghyn.
Vel glonney 'syn uinnag vooar nish?
Cha nel. Cha nel glonney erbee 'syn uinnag, agh ta ny claghyn mygeayrt ee ayn foast.
Cre hooar ronseyderyn raad va garey ny braaraghyn?
Hooar ad cro coull 'sy thalloo.
Cre cho mennick va ny braaraghyn ooashlaghey Jee?
Va ad ooashlaghey Jee shiaght keayrtyn dagh laa, ayns yn agglish.
Quoi ren screeu ayns oirr ny duillagyn?
Ren jeeaghteyr veih'n vannishter screeu mychione y sushtal ayns oirr ny duillagyn.
Cre ta'n mollaght gra?
T'eh gra: ‘Mollaght er quoi erbee ta goaill y lioar shoh ersooyl.’
Haink ny braaraghyn erash?
Cha daink. Cha daink ad erash dy bragh.

lessons.title: Lettyryn ny seihill
lessons.summary: Cosima Harcourt, an unpaid honorary professor in the languages department of the university in Douglas, has made an exhibition of the world's writing systems, and the student Severin Drew comes to see it: a clay tablet in the linear script Linear B, the argument about Linear A, the Semitic alphabets that the Greek and Latin alphabets came from, and an abugida from India, which Severin compares with the Manx alphabet. Cosima checked every word in the exhibition, and Severin has read her trilogy of murder stories.
lessons.text:
She olloo onnoroil ee Cosima Harcourt. T'ee three feed as hoght bleeaney d'eash, as t'ee gobbraghey 'sy rink çhengaghyn ec yn ollooscoill ayns Doolish. Myr olloo onnoroil, cha nel ee geddyn tuarastyl son yn obbyr, agh t'ee goll dys y rink dagh laa, son dy vel graih eck er çhengaghyn.

Nish ta taishbynys eck ayns y thie tashtee: “Lettyryn ny seihill.” Jiu, haink Severin Drew dy akin y taishbynys. She studeyr eh 'sy rink çhengaghyn, as t'eh feed as daa vlein d'eash.

Ayns y chied chishtey glonney, va peesh veg dy chray. “Ta'n screeu er y pheesh shoh ayns Linnagh B,” dooyrt Cosima. “Va Linnagh B jeant er ellan Creit, roish three thousane blein. Ta'n screeu linnagh: ta dagh cowrey jeant jeh linnaghyn giare, gyn cassanyn. She Greagish shenn y chengey t'ayn.”

“As ta screeu elley ayn, Linnagh A?” dooyrt Severin.

“Ta,” dooyrt Cosima. “Agh ta arganys mooar mychione Linnagh A. Cha nel fys ec peiagh erbee c'red ta'n chengey. Ta ronseyderyn ayn ta gra dy vel ee faggys da Greagish, as ronseyderyn elley ta gra nagh vel. Ta'n arganys goll er foast.”

Ayns y nah chishtey, va lettyryn semittagh. “Ta ny çhengaghyn semittagh, myr Arabish, screeuit veih'n laue yesh,” dooyrt Cosima. “Haink yn abbyrlhit Greagish veih lettyryn semittagh shenn, as haink yn abbyrlhit Ladjyn veih'n abbyrlhit Greagish. Myr shen, ta ny lettyryn ain hene çheet veih lettyryn semittagh.”

Ayns y trass chishtey, va abugida veih'n Injey. “Ayns abugida,” dooyrt Cosima, “ta dagh cowrey ny sheeloghe slane. Ta cowrey beg harrish y lettyr, ny fo, as t'eh caghlaa yn sheean.”

Ren Severin yn abugida y chosoyley rish yn abbyrlhit Gaelg. “Ta'n abugida ny s'giare,” dooyrt eh. “Ta mee cosoyley dagh fockle, as ta feme ec y Ghaelg er ny smoo dy lettyryn.”

“Ren mee feeraghey dagh fockle 'sy taishbynys,” dooyrt Cosima. “Ta feme ain er feeraghey dagh nhee, son dy vel ny sleih credjal ny focklyn er y voalley.”

Eisht dooyrt Severin: “Ta mee er lhaih yn treeskeealag eu!”

Ren Cosima gearey. Ta treeskeealag eck: three noaskeealyn mychione dunver. Ayns y chied lioar, ta dunver ec toghailt; 'sy nah lioar, ta dunver ayns thie lioaryn; as 'sy trass lioar, ta dunver ayns cashtal. “Ta'n treeskeealag aym linnagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta ny taghyrtyn ayns oardagh, veih'n chied dunver gys y jerrey.”

Ren Severin y chied lioar jeh'n treeskeealag y chur huic, as screeu ee e h-ennym ayn.

Feyshtyn:
Vel Cosima geddyn tuarastyl?
Cha nel. She olloo onnoroil ee, as cha nel ee geddyn tuarastyl son yn obbyr.
Cre'n fa ta Linnagh B linnagh?
Ta dagh cowrey jeant jeh linnaghyn giare, gyn cassanyn.
C'red ta'n arganys mychione Linnagh A?
Cha nel fys ec peiagh erbee c'red ta'n chengey.
Cre haink veih lettyryn semittagh shenn?
Haink yn abbyrlhit Greagish veih lettyryn semittagh shenn.
Cre ren Severin cosoyley rish yn abugida?
Ren eh yn abbyrlhit Gaelg y chosoyley rish yn abugida.
Ren Cosima feeraghey ny focklyn 'sy taishbynys?
Ren. Ren ee feeraghey dagh fockle.

lessons.title: Arran er aile moaney
lessons.summary: Aurelia Pentreath, eighty years old, plays an old farm woman of the 1880s in a cottage at the folk village in Cregneash, and nine-year-old Verity visits her: Aurelia bakes bread on a peat fire, explains how the neighbours cut peat together, why the poor soil needed seaweed, and why there is little vegetation on the hill; they see the cow and the ducks, and Verity, who first thought the old woman might be a witch, leaves fond of her.
lessons.text:
Ta Aurelia Pentreath kiare feed blein d'eash. Ayns y tourey, t'ee gobbraghey ayns thie beg shenn ayns Creneash, yn valley tashtee 'sy jiass. T'ee ceau eaddagh veih'n vlein 1880, as t'ee jannoo yn obbyr va mraane jannoo 'sy traa shen. Ta ny paitçhyn gra “y chaillagh” r'ee.

Er laa grianagh, haink inneen veg stiagh 'sy thie. She Verity yn ennym eck, as v'ee nuy bleeaney d'eash. Va Aurelia fuinney arran er yn aile.

“Vel oo ny caillagh?” dooyrt Verity. “Ny caillagh veih skeeal?”

Ren Aurelia gearey. “She caillagh mee, son dy vel mee shenn,” dooyrt ee. “Agh cha nel pooar erbee aym, agh pooar y fuinney!”

Va'n aile jeant jeh moain. “Cre ta moain?” dooyrt Verity.

“Ta moain çheet ass y thalloo fliugh er y chronk,” dooyrt Aurelia. “Va ny nabooyn goll seose er y chronk marish y cheilley 'sy tourey, as va dagh naboo giarey moain son dagh thie. Eisht va ny peeshyn moaney lhie 'sy ghrian, derrey v'ad çhirrym. Va aile moaney 'sy thie shoh, oie as laa, 'sy tourey as 'sy gheurey.”

Va'n fuinney er aile moaney doillee. Hug Aurelia yn arran ayns lhongey yiarn er yn aile, as hug ee moain çheh er y vullagh echey.

“Cre'n fa nagh row ny sleih gaase ny smoo dy vee?” dooyrt Verity.

“Va troaraght y thallooin beg ayns shoh,” dooyrt Aurelia. “Va creggyn 'sy thalloo, as va'n gheay veih'n faarkey feer lajer. Va ny sleih cur feamagh veih'n traie er y thalloo, son dy row troaraght ayns y feamagh. Lesh y feamagh, va troaraght ny smoo 'sy thalloo, as va praaseyn mie oc.”

Hie ad magh. Er y chronk, cha row monney glassyraght: agh faiyr giare as aittin. “Ta'n gheay ro lajer son glassyraght ard,” dooyrt Aurelia.

'Sy vagher, va booa ruy. “Va booa ec dagh thie,” dooyrt Aurelia. “Va'n bainney veih'n vooa scanshoil da ny paitçhyn.”

Ec y phoyll, va thunnagyn bane snaue. Hug Verity arran da ny thunnagyn. “Va oohyn thunnag mie son y fuinney,” dooyrt Aurelia.

Ec y jerrey, hug Aurelia peesh dy arran çheh da Verity. “Cha nel oo ny caillagh,” dooyrt Verity. “T'ou feer graihagh.”

“As t'ou uss graihagh neesht,” dooyrt Aurelia. “Tar erash, as bee oo ny naboo graihagh aym ayns Creneash.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta ny paitçhyn gra “y chaillagh” rish?
T'ad gra “y chaillagh” rish Aurelia Pentreath.
Cre va'n aile jeant jeh?
Va'n aile jeant jeh moain.
Quoi va giarey moain er y chronk?
Va ny nabooyn giarey moain marish y cheilley er y chronk.
Cre'n fa va ny sleih cur feamagh er y thalloo?
Va troaraght ayns y feamagh, as va troaraght y thallooin beg.
Vel monney glassyraght er y chronk?
Cha nel. Ta'n gheay ro lajer son glassyraght ard.
Cre honnick Verity 'sy vagher as ec y phoyll?
Honnick ee booa ruy 'sy vagher, as thunnagyn bane ec y phoyll.
Cre dooyrt Verity rish Aurelia ec y jerrey?
Dooyrt ee: “T'ou feer graihagh.”

lessons.title: Lettyryn veih'n champ
lessons.summary: Anneliese Moser from England reads her grandfather's letters in the museum archive in Douglas: in 1940 Gustav, a German citizen who had lived in London for ten years, was taken by policemen with a warrant and interned in a camp of seafront boarding houses in Douglas, though he had committed no crime. His wife Liesl and their baby, dependent on him for money, stayed in London, where Liesl was hurt when a bomb fell on their street; but the camp brought some good too, and in 1941 Gustav went home.
lessons.text:
Ta Anneliese Moser cummal ayns Sostyn. Ayns 1940, va'n shennayr eck, Gustav Moser, cummal ayns Lunnin. V'eh ny seyranagh jeh'n Ghermaan, agh v'eh er ve cummal ayns Lunnin rish jeih bleeaney, marish e ven, Liesl.

Jiu, ta Anneliese ayns y tashtlann 'sy thie tashtee ayns Doolish. Ta lettyryn Gustav ayns y tashtlann nish, as t'ee lhaih ad son y chied cheayrt.

Ta'n chied lettyr veih Boaldyn 1940. Screeu Gustav eh da Liesl veih'n champ:

“Haink poleenyn dys y thie ain lesh barrant. Dooyrt y barrant dy row orrym goll lhieu, son dy vel mee ny seyranagh jeh'n Ghermaan. Cha nel loght erbee aym. Cha ren mee rieau red erbee olk.”

Ayns 1940, va caggey eddyr Sostyn as y Ghermaan. Va aggle er y reiltys roish dagh seyranagh jeh'n Ghermaan ayns Sostyn. Hug ad ymmodee jeu dys campyn ayns Mannin, ga nagh row loght erbee orroo. Cha row agh barrant beg pabyr ec ny poleenyn, agh va pooar mooar ayns y barrant shen.

Ta'n nah lettyr veih'n champ ayns Doolish: “Ta'n champ jeant jeh thieyn oast er y traie, as ta yiarn mygeayrt orroo. Ta barney eddyr daa hie, as trooid y barney shen ta mee fakin y faarkey dagh moghrey. Ta mee smooinaghtyn ort as er y lhiannoo. T'ou crogheydagh orrym son argid, as cha nod mee obbraghey ayns shoh. Ta shen y red smoo doillee.”

Ta lettyr veih Liesl ayns y tashtlann neesht. V'ee crogheydagh er argid veih'n reiltys, as er e naboo. “Ta bleaystanyn tuittym er Lunnin dagh oie,” screeu ee. “Huitt bleaystan er y traid ain Jesarn s'jerree. Va mee gortit, agh cha row mee feer gortit, as cha row y lhiannoo gortit. Ta'n bleaystan er jannoo towl mooar 'sy traid.”

Agh va foays ayns y champ neesht. Ayns y trass lettyr, screeu Gustav: “Ta ellyneyryn as ynseyderyn ayns y champ shoh. T'ad jannoo lessoonyn son ny deiney elley. Ta mee ynsaghey Baarle as kiaull. Ta foays mooar ayn dooin ooilley.”

'Sy vlein 1941, va Gustav lhiggit ass y champ, as hie eh erash dys Lunnin, dys Liesl as y lhiannoo. Ayns y lettyr s'jerree, screeu eh: “Va'n traa shoh doillee, agh hooar mee foays ass. Bee mee cooinaghtyn er y barney eddyr ny thieyn, as er y faarkey, son dy bragh.”

Feyshtyn:
Row Gustav ny seyranagh jeh Sostyn?
Cha row. V'eh ny seyranagh jeh'n Ghermaan, agh v'eh cummal ayns Lunnin.
Cre va ec ny poleenyn?
Va barrant ec ny poleenyn.
Row loght erbee er Gustav?
Cha row. Cha ren eh rieau red erbee olk.
Cre va Gustav fakin trooid y barney?
V'eh fakin y faarkey trooid y barney eddyr daa hie.
Cre'n fa va Liesl crogheydagh er argid veih'n reiltys?
Va Gustav 'sy champ, as cha row eh abyl obbraghey.
Row Liesl gortit tra huitt y bleaystan?
Va, agh cha row ee feer gortit.

lessons.title: Yn thie oast faggys da'n railley
lessons.summary: Isadora Ackroyd, who works in architecture, and the builder Wendell Godwin restore an old hotel in Douglas, built in 1890 near the railway station in the style of the Italian Renaissance: they mend cracks in the curved marble staircase with resin, put iron bands round a wall that has a structural problem, and replace the broken drainage with flexible new pipes; old buildings have disadvantages, but when the hotel opens again the marble shines as it did in 1890.
lessons.text:
Ta Isadora Ackroyd gobbraghey ayns troggalaght. T'ee aahroggal thieyn shenn, as s'mie lhee troggalaght shenn ny share na troggalaght noa. Ayns y vlein shoh, t'ee gobbraghey er thie oast mooar ayns Doolish, faggys da stashoon y railley. Ta troggeyder gobbraghey marish: Wendell Godwin.

Va'n thie oast troggit 'sy vlein 1890. 'Sy traa shen, va'n railley noa, as va sleih çheet er y railley veih Purt ny h-Inshey as veih Rhumsaa dy chadley 'sy thie oast as dy gholl dys y traie.

“Ta troggalaght y thie shoh ayns aght yn Aaruggyr,” dooyrt Isadora rish Wendell. “Haink y troggalaght shen veih'n Iddaal, veih traa yn Aaruggyr, roish queig cheead blein. Jeeagh er ny uinnagyn ard, as er y mullagh: she aght yn Aaruggyr t'ayn.”

Stiagh 'sy thie, va staartey mooar jeant jeh marmyr bane. Va'n staartey lhoobagh: v'eh goll seose myr cassan lhoobagh, gyn corneil erbee. Haink y marmyr veih'n Iddaal er lhong. Agh nish, va scoltaghyn 'sy marmyr.

“Cre nee shin?” dooyrt Wendell.

“Ver shin rosin 'sy scoltey,” dooyrt Isadora. “Ta'n rosin çheet veih biljyn. T'eh bog ec y toshiaght, as eisht t'eh goll creoi. Cha bee'n rosin ry akin 'sy marmyr.” Ren Wendell lhieeney dagh scoltey lesh rosin, dy kiart as dy meein.

Va doilleeid troggalagh ayn neesht. Va boalley mooar ec cooyl y thie goll magh, beggan as beggan. “She doilleeid troggalagh eh shoh,” dooyrt Isadora. “Ta feme ain er obbyr troggalagh roish my vees y thie sauçhey.” Hug ad boandey yiarn mygeayrt y voalley, as boandey elley harrish y chied boandey. Ren y daa voandey yiarn y boalley y chummal ayns e ynnyd.

Eisht, hie ad sheese fo'n thie. Va'n sornaigys shenn brisht, as va ushtey 'sy thalloo fo'n thie. “Ta'n sornaigys shoh veih'n vlein 1890 neesht,” dooyrt Wendell. Ren ad yn sornaigys shenn y ghoaill ersooyl, as hug ad feddanyn noa ayn. Va ny feddanyn noa lhoobagh: v'ad goll mygeayrt ny claghyn gyn brishey.

“Ta neuvondeish ec thie shenn,” dooyrt Wendell. “T'eh feayr, as ta'n obbyr deyr.”

“Ta,” dooyrt Isadora. “Agh ta neuvondeish ec thie noa neesht: cha nel shennaghys erbee echey.”

Ayns Mean Fouyir, va'n thie oast foshlit reesht. Va'n staartey marmyr bane as gial, myr v'eh 'sy vlein 1890.

Feyshtyn:
Raad ta'n thie oast?
Ta'n thie oast ayns Doolish, faggys da stashoon y railley.
Cre'n aght troggalaght t'ayns y thie?
She aght yn Aaruggyr t'ayn, veih'n Iddaal.
Cre ren Wendell 'sy scoltey 'sy marmyr?
Ren eh lhieeney dagh scoltey lesh rosin.
Cre hug ad mygeayrt y voalley?
Hug ad boandey yiarn mygeayrt y voalley.
Cre'n fa va ny feddanyn noa mie?
Va ny feddanyn noa lhoobagh, as v'ad goll mygeayrt ny claghyn gyn brishey.
Cre'n neuvondeish t'ec thie shenn?
T'eh feayr, as ta'n obbyr deyr.

lessons.title: Bluckan golf er yn eayst
lessons.summary: Cornelius Fanshawe, a retired aeroplane engineer, takes his twelve-year-old grandson Jago to an exhibition on the history of space travel in Douglas: they see part of a real rocket, learn that orbits are elliptical like an egg, and that the terrestrial planets are made of rock and scientists look for potential ones round other stars; they see a copy of the golf ball that a golfer hit on the Moon in 1971, and hear of a senator who flew in space again at seventy-seven while researchers measured how fast his muscles grew weak.
lessons.text:
Ta Cornelius Fanshawe three feed as queig jeig d'eash. Rish daeed blein, v'eh gobbraghey er etlanyn. Jiu, t'eh goll lesh e oe, Jago, dys taishbynys mychione shennaghys y spoar ayns Doolish. Ta Jago daa vlein jeig d'eash.

Ayns y chied shamyr, va ayrn jeh roggad feer. V'eh ard, myr thie mooar. “Hug y roggad shoh lhong-spoar seose 'syn aer,” dooyrt Cornelius. “Ta aile mooar ec bun y roggad, as t'eh goll seose dy tappee. Lurg tammylt, ta'n roggad tuittym ersooyl, as ta'n lhong-spoar goll er e raad hene.”

Er y voalley, va jalloo jeh'n Chruinney, as linney mygeayrt ee. “Cha nel y chruinlagh cruinn,” dooyrt Cornelius. “T'ee eelipsagh, myr ooh. Ren Kepler feddyn magh dy vel cruinleeyn ny planaidyn mygeayrt y ghrian eelipsagh neesht.”

Ayns y nah shamyr, va ny planaidyn. “Ta kiare planaidyn ooirragh ayn,” dooyrt Cornelius: “Mercur, Venus, y Chruinney as Mart. Ta ny planaidyn ooirragh jeant jeh creg. Cha nel Jupiter ooirragh: t'eh jeant jeh gas, son y chooid smoo.”

“Vel planaidyn ooirragh elley ayn, mygeayrt rollageyn elley?” dooyrt Jago.

“Ta ronseyderyn shirrey ad nish,” dooyrt Cornelius. “T'ad er feddyn ymmodee planaidyn cummyssagh: planaidyn raad foddee bea ve. Agh cha nel fys ain foast. Ta dagh planaid cummyssagh foddey ersooyl.”

Ayns y trass shamyr, va bluckan beg bane fo glonney. “She bluckan golf eh shoh!” dooyrt Jago.

“She coip t'ayn,” dooyrt Cornelius. “Ayns 1971, va golfeyr mie ny oltey jeh'n phossan va goll dys yn eayst. Ren y golfeyr shen bwoailley bluckan golf er yn eayst. Son dy vel yn eayst beg, hie yn bluckan foddey, foddey.”

Er y boalley elley, va jalloo jeh dooinney shenn. “Va'n dooinney shoh ny shannadeyr 'sy Steatyn Unnaneysit,” dooyrt Cornelius. “Tra v'eh aeg, hie eh dys y spoar. Eisht, v'eh ny shannadeyr rish feed as kiare bleeaney. Tra v'eh three feed as shiaght jeig d'eash, hie'n shannadeyr dys y spoar reesht.”

“Cre'n fa?” dooyrt Jago.

“Son dy vel muskylyn goll lag 'sy spoar,” dooyrt Cornelius. “Ta ny muskylyn coayl nyn niart er reat tappee 'sy spoar, myr ta muskylyn sleih shenn coayl nyn niart er y Chruinney. Ren ny ronseyderyn towse yn reat echey: reat y chree, as reat coayl ny muskylyn.”

“Ta mee laccal goll dys y spoar,” dooyrt Jago.

“Eisht bee feme ayd er muskylyn lajer,” dooyrt Cornelius, as ren eh gearey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va 'sy chied shamyr?
Va ayrn jeh roggad feer 'sy chied shamyr.
Vel y chruinlagh cruinn?
Cha nel. T'ee eelipsagh, myr ooh.
Cre ta ny planaidyn ooirragh jeant jeh?
Ta ny planaidyn ooirragh jeant jeh creg.
Cre ta planaid cummyssagh?
She planaid cummyssagh planaid raad foddee bea ve.
Cre ren y golfeyr er yn eayst?
Ren eh bwoailley bluckan golf er yn eayst.
Cre'n fa hie'n shannadeyr dys y spoar reesht?
Son dy vel muskylyn goll lag 'sy spoar, as ren ny ronseyderyn towse y reat echey.

lessons.title: Kishtey yn ronseyder
lessons.summary: Romilly Garrick, who does restoration work in the museum in Douglas, opens the old cabinet of a Victorian naturalist with ten-year-old Lucan, who is spending a week with her: inside are a bird of prey that looks alive, the skull and hairy skin of an ape, a sea sponge that is an animal and not a plant, fossil shells, the traps the naturalist used for mice and insects, a glass slide showing a cell with its endoplasmic reticulum, and a small glass tube of insulin, a hormone, from his grandson the doctor.
lessons.text:
Ta Romilly Garrick gobbraghey 'sy thie tashtee ayns Doolish. T'ee jannoo obbyr aavioghee: t'ee aavioghey reddyn shenn, myr eaddagh, lioaryn as craueyn, as t'ee freayll ad sauçhey. Ta'n obbyr aavioghee meein as liauyr. Ta Lucan, guilley jeih bleeaney d'eash, marish ee rish shiaghtin. T'eh laccal ynsaghey mychione yn obbyr eck.

Jiu, ren Romilly kishtey mooar shenn y osley. Va'n kishtey ec ronseyder ennagh veih'n nuyoo eash jeig, as va reddyn jeh dagh sorçh ayn.

Va shirragh ayns y chied ayrn jeh'n kishtey. Va'n shirragh marroo rish keead blein, agh v'eh jeeaghyn bio, as e chassyn creoi as e hooill buigh. “Ta'n shirragh shelg cretooryn beggey, myr y lugh,” dooyrt Romilly. “Ta feme er obbyr aavioghee er y shirragh shoh: ta'n daah echey goll ersooyl.”

'Sy nah ayrn, va claigin ape, as crackan renaigagh. “Va'n ape shoh veih'n Affrick,” dooyrt Romilly. “Jeeagh, ta'n crackan renaigagh, as ta'n folt doo as liauyr.” Va duillag renaigagh veih lus elley 'sy kishtey neesht. Ren Lucan bentyn rish y duillag. V'ee renaigagh as bog.

Eisht hooar Lucan red buigh as eddrym, as towlyn beggey ooilley harrish. “C'red ta shoh? Vel eh ny lus?”

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Romilly. “She faastguin eh. Ta faastguin bio 'sy faarkey. She cretoor eh, cha nel eh ny lus. Va sleih goaill ymmyd jeh faastguin son glenney.”

Ayns kishtey beg, va shliggyn fossylagh. V'ad jeant jeh creg. “Ta ny shliggyn fossylagh shoh shenn, shenn,” dooyrt Romilly. “Va ny cretooryn bio 'sy faarkey roish millioonyn dy vleeantyn.”

Va ribbey ayn neesht, jeant jeh fuygh as yiarn. “Va'n ronseyder goaill ymmyd jeh'n ribbey shoh son geddyn y lugh,” dooyrt Romilly. “As va ribbey glonney echey son ny feeaghyn ec yn oie.”

Ec y jerrey, hooar ad peesh glonney eddrym, as jalloo beg er. Hug Romilly fo scaalhean eh. “She killag t'ayn,” dooyrt ee. “Jeeagh: shoh yn çheshvean, as shoh yn moggyl endoplasmagh mygeayrt. Ta'n moggyl endoplasmagh jannoo proteenyn son y killag.”

Va feddan glonney beg 'sy kishtey neesht, veih 1923. “Haink shoh veih oe y ronseyder, va ny fer lhee,” dooyrt Romilly. “She insulin eh. She broddag insulin. Ta'n broddag shoh freayll y shugyr 'sy fuill kiart.”

“S'mie lhiam obbyr aavioghee,” dooyrt Lucan. “Tra vees mee ny smoo, bee mee jannoo yn obbyr shoh.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr ta Romilly jannoo?
T'ee jannoo obbyr aavioghee 'sy thie tashtee.
Cre'n fa ta feme er obbyr aavioghee er y shirragh?
Ta'n daah echey goll ersooyl.
Row'n crackan ape renaigagh?
Va. Va'n crackan renaigagh, as va'n folt doo as liauyr.
Vel faastguin ny lus?
Cha nel. She cretoor eh ta bio 'sy faarkey.
Cre va'n ronseyder jannoo lesh y ribbey?
V'eh goaill ymmyd jeh'n ribbey son geddyn y lugh.
Cre va ny shliggyn fossylagh jeant jeh?
Va ny shliggyn fossylagh jeant jeh creg.
Cre ta'n moggyl endoplasmagh jannoo?
T'eh jannoo proteenyn son y killag.
Cre ta insulin?
She broddag eh, ta freayll y shugyr 'sy fuill kiart.

lessons.title: Ny bluckanyn fedjagagh
lessons.summary: The journalist Ianthe Wolverton visits Constance Featherstone, ninety, who won the island's badminton contest in 1955: over tea and almonds Constance shows her old racket and the feathered shuttlecocks of the time, explains that a promoter who owned hotels in Douglas proposed the contest in the years of the island's prosperity, describes the final, where her last shot was deliberate, and tells how her husband proposed to her after the match; today's shuttlecocks are plastic, but she keeps the feathered ones.
lessons.text:
Ta Ianthe Wolverton screeu son pabyr naight ayns Doolish. Jiu, t'ee goll dy akin Constance Featherstone, ben kiare feed as jeih bleeaney d'eash. 'Sy vlein 1955, ren Constance cosney yn tostyl badmyntyn mooar ayns Mannin.

Hug Constance tey as almonyn er y voayrd. “Gow almon,” dooyrt ee. “S'mie lhiam almonyn. Va almonyn ain 'sy vlein 1955 neesht, lurg y tostyl.”

Er y voayrd, va maidjey badmyntyn shenn, jeant jeh fuygh, as kishtey beg. 'Sy kishtey, va bluckanyn fedjagagh. “Va ny bluckanyn badmyntyn fedjagagh 'sy traa shen,” dooyrt Constance. “Nish, ta ny bluckanyn jeant jeh stoo plastagh. Ta'n bluckan plastagh lajer, as cha nel eh deyr. Agh va'n bluckan fedjagagh ny share. V'eh goll dy meein, myr ushag.”

“Quoi ren y tostyl y stiurey?” dooyrt Ianthe.

“Greeseyder veih Doolish,” dooyrt Constance. “Va thieyn oast echey er y traie. 'Sy traa shen, va speeideilys mooar ayns Mannin. Va thousaneyn dy leih çheet veih Sostyn dagh tourey, as va argid ec dy chooilley pheiagh. Ayns y speeideilys shen, ren y greeseyder treeal tostyl badmyntyn son ny h-ellanee. Dooyrt eh dy jinnagh y tostyl sleih y chur stiagh 'sy thie oast echey. As ren eh!”

“Kys va'n tostyl hene?”

“Va kiare feed cloieder ayn,” dooyrt Constance. “'Sy chloie s'jerree, va mish as ben veih Rhumsaa cloie. Va'n cloie liauyr as doillee. Ec y jerrey, ren mee bwoailley yn bluckan dy meein, harrish y lieen, gys yn corneil. Cha row eh ny haghyrt: v'eh keayllagh. Ren mee y bwoalley shen dy keayllagh, son dy row fys aym dy row y ven elley lag.”

“As cre haghyr lurg y tostyl?”

Ren Constance gearey. “Va dooinney aeg 'sy theay, Leander. Lurg y tostyl, haink eh hym lesh blaaghyn. Ren eh treeal dy beagh shin poost! Dooyrt mee ‘ta,’ as va shin poost rish three feed blein. As hug y greeseyder almonyn dooin son y phoosey!”

Ec y jerrey, hug Constance bluckan fedjagagh da Ianthe. “Freill eh,” dooyrt ee. “Cha nel bluckan plastagh erbee cho aalin.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren Constance cosney 'sy vlein 1955?
Ren ee cosney yn tostyl badmyntyn mooar ayns Mannin.
Cre va ny bluckanyn jeant jeh 'sy traa shen?
V'ad fedjagagh. Nish, t'ad jeant jeh stoo plastagh.
Quoi ren treeal y tostyl?
Ren greeseyder veih Doolish treeal y tostyl.
Cre'n fa va argid ec sleih 'sy traa shen?
Va speeideilys mooar ayns Mannin, as va thousaneyn dy leih çheet veih Sostyn.
Row'n bwoalley s'jerree keayllagh?
Va. Ren Constance y bwoalley shen dy keayllagh.
Cre hug Constance er y voayrd?
Hug ee tey as almonyn er y voayrd.
